title: AP CSP — Lesson 19 Homework: Procedures & Libraries
notice: All questions are original. Q1–Q6 are AP-style practice, not official AP questions. Q7–Q12 and all marks are teacher-designed. Q5 earns one mark only for both correct choices and no others. Q5: select exactly TWO. Procedure definitions and library contracts are supplied in the question. RETURN sends a value to the caller; DISPLAY produces output. Put braces on separate lines.

questions.prompt: How many times does FOR EACH run its body for an empty list?
questions.explanation: A follows zero elements. B invents a visit. C incorrectly retains a previous input. D assumes indexing not required by FOR EACH.

questions.prompt: A supplied procedure toHours(m) returns m / 60. What does toHours(150) return?
questions.explanation: C is 150/60. A returns the input; B truncates decimal division; D subtracts 60 without instruction.

questions.prompt: For PROCEDURE combine(left, right), the call is combine(4, 9). Which statement is correct?

options.label: D
options.text: Both parameters must be named combine.

questions.explanation: B binds arguments by position. A confuses values with names. C reverses order. D confuses procedure and parameter names.

questions.prompt: A procedure only DISPLAYs a number and has no RETURN. What can its caller safely assume?

options.label: A
options.text: The displayed number is its returned numeric value.

options.label: D
options.text: Output is produced, but no numeric return is promised.

questions.explanation: D distinguishes the effect from a returned result. A invents a return contract. B confuses procedure flow with program termination. C ignores DISPLAY.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements are true? Select exactly TWO answers.

options.label: A
options.text: A parameter can let one procedure work with varied inputs.

options.label: B
options.text: Calling a library removes the need to read its documentation.

options.label: C
options.text: A procedure definition executes its body immediately.

options.label: D
options.text: Documentation can specify parameters and returned values.

questions.explanation: A supports generalization. D describes useful API documentation. B ignores the need to understand behavior. C confuses defining with calling.

questions.prompt: Inside a procedure, RETURN(6) is executed before DISPLAY(99). What happens?

options.label: B
options.text: 6 is returned and that later DISPLAY is skipped.

options.label: D
options.text: Every remaining caller statement is skipped.

questions.explanation: B reflects immediate return from the current call. A and C execute unreachable code. D incorrectly ends the entire caller, which can continue.

questions.prompt: toHours(m) returns m/60; reachedGoal(m,g) returns m ≥ g. Give (a) toHours(45), (b) toHours(120), (c) reachedGoal(30, 30), and (d) reachedGoal(30, 45).
Write a procedure toHours(minutes) that returns minutes/60. Then write one call that assigns its result for 90 minutes to hours. Do not print inside the procedure.

rubric.criterion: minutes is the input parameter used in the calculation.
Returns minutes/60 rather than only displaying it.
Calls toHours(90) and assigns its result to hours.

questions.prompt: Write reachedGoal(minutes, goal) to return whether minutes ≥ goal. Then assign reachedGoal(20, 30) to met. Use both parameters; do not hard-code a fixed target.

rubric.criterion: Defines both parameters in the named procedure.
Compares minutes ≥ goal inclusively using the parameters.
Correct two-argument call assigned to met.

questions.prompt: A procedure demo executes RETURN(8) and then contains DISPLAY(99). A caller evaluates result ← demo() + 2. Give (a) the returned value, (b) whether 99 is displayed, (c) why the later statement is skipped, and (d) result.
questions.answer: (a) 8. (b) No. (c) RETURN immediately transfers control back to the caller. (d) 10.
questions.explanation: (a) 8. (b) No. (c) RETURN immediately transfers control back to the caller. (d) 10.

rubric.criterion: Explains immediate return from the current procedure call.

questions.prompt: Fictional DurationKit provides seconds(m): m is a nonnegative number of minutes; it returns numeric seconds and produces no display output. State (a) its input unit, (b) returned unit, (c) seconds(2.5), and (d) whether a separate DISPLAY is needed to show that result.
questions.answer: (a) Minutes. (b) Seconds. (c) 150. (d) Yes: use DISPLAY(seconds(2.5)) or display a stored returned result.
questions.explanation: (a) Minutes. (b) Seconds. (c) 150. (d) Yes: use DISPLAY(seconds(2.5)) or display a stored returned result.

rubric.criterion: A separate caller DISPLAY is required to show the value.

questions.prompt: A program copies the same goal comparison into three features. (a) Name a reusable helper. (b) Propose its two parameters. (c) Explain one maintenance benefit. (d) State the condition under which changing its internals need not change its callers.
questions.answer: (a) reachedGoal. (b) minutes and goal. (c) Shared comparison logic can be maintained in one body instead of three copies. (d) Preserve the documented inputs, returned meaning and other promised behavior.
questions.explanation: (a) reachedGoal. (b) minutes and goal. (c) Shared comparison logic can be maintained in one body instead of three copies. (d) Preserve the documented inputs, returned meaning and other promised behavior.

rubric.criterion: Two parameters representing observed minutes and target.
Concrete reduction of duplicated logic or one-place maintenance.
Requires preserving the caller-visible contract, not arbitrary changes.
